leanness.title: Facial leanness (facial fat / bloat)
leanness.why: The strongest, most reliable predictor of ratings in the reference data. Fuller faces (wider cheeks relative to height, jaw rounded by fat) rate lower.
actions: Get to roughly 10-15% body fat (men) / 18-25% (women) with a moderate calorie deficit (~300-500 kcal/day) and high protein (1.6-2.2 g/kg)
Lift weights 3x/week while dieting so the weight lost is fat, not muscle
Cut alcohol, especially in the days before photos or events: it causes facial puffiness and redness
Keep sodium steady and potassium high (vegetables, beans, potatoes): big salt spikes cause next-day water retention in the face
Sleep 7-9 h; short sleep makes faces look puffier and less healthy

eyes.title: Eye area (eye size vs spacing, brow position)
eyes.why: Larger-looking eyes relative to the gap between them, and brows set closer to the eyes ('hunter eyes'), go with higher ratings. Bone and soft tissue set most of this.
actions: Fix sleep and allergies first: dark circles and puffy lids make eyes look smaller
Keep brows full, especially the lower edge; only remove strays and the unibrow. Over-plucking raises the brow line visually
Lower body fat: fat around the orbit and upper lid reduces visible eye area
Pick glasses that do not shrink the eyes (strong minus lenses do; ask about high-index lenses, or consider contacts)
Clinical option for marked eyelid hooding or lower-lid issues: oculoplastic surgeon consultation, never DIY

lower_third.title: Chin and lower third
lower_third.why: A longer chin relative to the philtrum (lip-to-nose distance) goes with higher ratings. Community target ~2:1 chin-to-philtrum; the reference median is about 2.0.
actions: Men: grow heavy stubble or a short beard shaped longer at the chin and clean under the jawline; this visually lengthens and squares the chin
Keep a clean neckline (trim below the jaw) so the jaw-neck angle reads sharper
Lose fat under the chin before judging your chin; submental fat hides projection
See an orthodontist if your bite is off; jaw position and lip support change with it
Clinical options for a genuinely recessed chin: genioplasty or chin implant (board-certified surgeon). Fillers are temporary.

midface.title: Midface proportions
midface.why: A compact midface (shorter distance from eyes to mouth relative to eye spacing) goes with slightly higher ratings for men. This is skeletal.
actions: Moustache/stubble on the upper lip visually shortens a long philtrum
Hairstyles with some volume on top and fuller sides balance a long midface
Skeletal changes need orthognathic surgery for a real functional problem (bite, airway), assessed by a maxillofacial surgeon

symmetry.title: Symmetry
symmetry.why: More symmetric faces rate slightly higher. Most asymmetry is skeletal or dental; some is soft tissue and habit.
actions: Use a side part toward the fuller side of the face; asymmetric hair hides asymmetry better than a centre part
Chew on both sides; one-sided chewing can enlarge one masseter
Sleep on your back if you can; face-down sleeping adds one-sided creases over years
Find your better side for photos (take both and compare)
Dental check if your bite or smile is crooked

harmony.title: Harmony (closeness to the average face)
harmony.why: Faces close to the population average rate higher. This is mostly bone structure; framing (hair, beard, glasses) changes how proportions read.
actions: Ask a good barber for a cut that balances your face shape (e.g. more height for round faces, fuller sides for long faces)
Use facial hair to correct proportions: chin length for a short lower third, fuller sides for a narrow face
Glasses frames roughly as wide as the face and following the brow line

skin.title: Skin quality
skin.why: Even tone and smooth texture are among the strongest cues in the research literature. The tool's photo-based skin score is crude, so trust the mirror too.
actions: Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen SPF 30+, every morning, all year
Gentle cleanser + moisturiser; do not over-wash
A retinoid at night (adapalene OTC, or tretinoin by prescription) for acne, texture and ageing. Start 2-3x/week; avoid in pregnancy
Persistent acne, scarring or rosacea: see a dermatologist; prescription treatment works far better than product-hopping
Eat plenty of colourful fruit and vegetables: carotenoids give skin a golden tone that raters read as healthy
Do not smoke; it is one of the clearest causes of premature facial ageing

dimorphism.title: Sex-typical features
dimorphism.why: For women, more feminine face shapes rated clearly higher; for men, masculinity showed almost no link to ratings in the reference data.
actions: Men: lean out and use stubble to define the jaw, rather than chasing extreme masculinity
Women: brow shape, hairstyle and makeup technique strongly change how feminine a face reads

presentation: Head angle: tilt your head very slightly down and look into the lens. In the reference data head pitch alone correlated ~0.5 with ratings, more than any facial measure
Never take close selfies at arm's length: at ~30 cm, the lens makes the nose look about 30% bigger than at 1.5 m. Use a timer or a friend with the camera at 1.5-2 m
Soft light from the front or slightly above (window light). Hard overhead light deepens under-eye shadows
Camera at or slightly above eye level; below the chin widens the jaw and neck
Neutral expression or slight closed-mouth smile; wide open-mouth smiles rated lower in the reference data
Keep a fresh haircut (every 3-5 weeks for short styles) and clothes that fit at the shoulders
core_habits: Sleep 7-9 hours on a regular schedule
Sleep-deprived faces are rated less attractive and less healthy (Axelsson et al., BMJ 2010).
Builds shoulder-to-waist ratio and upper-body strength cues, which strongly drive male body attractiveness, and helps facial leanness.
Slows visible skin ageing (randomised trial, Hughes et al. 2013).
High-protein, mostly whole-food diet at a body fat that shows your bone structure
Helps fat loss and circulation (skin colour).
Good posture: stack head over shoulders
Forward head posture softens the jaw-neck angle in profile.
Teeth: whitening (dentist-supervised) and straightening if needed
lesser_known: Carotenoid-rich diet (carrots, sweet potato, tomatoes, peppers, leafy greens)
Raises skin yellowness within ~6-8 weeks; raters read it as healthier and more attractive than a tan (Stephen, Whitehead et al.).
Close lenses inflate nose size about 30% (Ward et al., JAMA Facial Plast Surg 2018).
Treat nasal congestion / allergies / sleep apnoea
Better sleep and less under-eye puffiness; chronic mouth-breathing in children is linked to longer faces. In adults it will not move bone, but breathing and sleep improve.
Heavy stubble over clean-shaven for most men
Heavy stubble often rates highest in studies (Dixson & Brooks 2013), but preferences vary.
Keep brows thick; trim instead of plucking the lower edge
Lower, fuller brows make the eye area look deeper ('hunter eyes').
Cold water or a cold compress in the morning
Temporarily reduces puffiness; lasts hours, not days.
Sleep on your back with your head slightly raised
Less morning eyelid puffiness and fewer sleep creases.
Ferritin / iron, vitamin D and thyroid check if hair is shedding
Common, treatable causes of hair thinning; ask a doctor for bloodwork.
Controls dandruff and scalp inflammation; small evidence as a hair-loss adjunct.
Hair loss: talk to a doctor early about minoxidil / finasteride
Both work and are most effective when started early. Prescription only; finasteride has known side effects that need to be discussed with a doctor.
Temporary depuffing at best; does not change fat or bone.
overrated: Mewing (tongue posture) to reshape the adult jaw
No credible evidence it changes adult bone. Good tongue posture is harmless; holding the jaw forward can cause jaw pain.
Hard-gum chewing (mastic) for a bigger jaw
May enlarge masseters slightly, but can strain the jaw joint (TMJ pain, clicking).
Canthal tilt as a key rating factor
In the reference data, its apparent link to ratings disappeared once head angle was controlled.
Facial exercises / 'face yoga' to slim the face
You cannot spot-reduce facial fat; overall fat loss is what works.
avoid: Bone smashing (hitting facial bones to 'remodel' them)
No evidence; risks fractures, nerve damage, asymmetric scarring and vision damage.
DNP or other unregulated fat-loss drugs
DNP has killed people at doses close to the 'effective' dose.
Non-prescribed steroids, SARMs, or other hormones
Cardiovascular, liver and fertility harm; can accelerate hair loss and cause acne.
Melanotan / tanning injections, and tanning beds
Unregulated peptides and UV beds raise skin-cancer risk.
DIY fillers, injections, 'thumb pulling' or home palate expanders
Infection, vascular occlusion, dental and joint damage.
Makes the face gaunt, loses muscle, causes hair shedding; weight rebounds.
surgical_note: Structural changes (chin, jaw, nose, eyelids, orthognathic surgery) are only safe with a board-certified surgeon after an in-person consultation. Get a second opinion, and prefer treating a functional issue (bite, airway) over a purely aesthetic one.

cheek_jaw: higher = more taper from cheekbones to jaw
intercanthal_eye_ratio: lower = eyes larger relative to the gap
